evidence.description: Re-read all 18 slot entries fresh; confirmed zero 'risk' or 'alwaysAvailable' fields exist anywhere in the file today, including on economy/gig, economy/ubi, and every self/* slot that REQ-201's own EARS clause names as slots that must remain visible to a broke instance.

Confirmed REQ-201's default-value fix (FIND-001) and alwaysAvailableOf mechanism (FIND-002) are both genuinely landed and internally consistent with each other, but their interaction with the untagged-slot fail-closed-by-default edge case creates a new, concrete contradiction against the requirement's own worked example (FIND-101).
Re-read liquidityDirective in full; confirmed the FIND-003 narrative (COMPUTE_RESERVE_USDC-triggered close-or-withdraw steer) is accurately described in the revised REQ-201 carve-out text.

Re-read acquire()/withGigLock(); confirmed REQ-101's now-binding isLockStale extraction requirement, once implemented, would make the Tier-1 purity claim true of the actual code (FIND-004 genuinely resolved).

Read the actual positionsSummary computation (lines 243-247): filters recentLedger strictly to entries whose source startsWith('yield'); confirmed this structurally excludes all hl_trade activity, contradicting verification-architecture.md's claim that hasOpenRiskPositionOf reads 'the same underlying position bookkeeping that populates ctx.positionsSummary today' (FIND-102).

Confirmed the only code that actually knows live HL open-position state is a real Hyperliquid clearinghouseState network call inside the hl_trade skill's own script, not surfaced to index.mjs/context.mjs/filterCatalog anywhere today -- the new bookkeeping signal this increment relies on for its fund-safety carve-out does not yet exist and its failure mode is entirely unspecified.
Re-read the full file (lines 1-234); confirmed the FIND-005 baseline correction is accurate and REQ-204's target phrases are quoted correctly at the cited line range.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-201's fail-closed-by-default rule for untagged registry.json slots, combined with the real, current registry.json (which has zero risk/alwaysAvailable tags on economy/gig, economy/ubi, or any self/* slot), means a criteria-satisfying Phase 3 implementation would hide economy/gig -- the exact $0-capital earn mechanism broke instances are supposed to use -- from every broke instance, directly contradicting REQ-201's own EARS clause and this increment's stated purpose.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: The requirement is not implementable as a single, unambiguous, self-consistent target: literal compliance with the acceptance criteria breaks the requirement's own stated intent and the feature's headline bootstrap scenario the moment the gate ships.

blockingFindings.summary: hasOpenRiskPositionOf is specified as reading 'already-fetched' position bookkeeping identical to ctx.positionsSummary, but positionsSummary today structurally excludes all hl_trade data (yield-only filter). The real HL position signal requires a brand-new, unspecified live network dependency with an entirely unaddressed failure mode (fail-open defeats the gate; fail-closed can reopen the exact FIND-003 deadlock this carve-out claims to close).
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A purity/data-flow claim central to this revision's headline fix (FIND-003) does not match the real code it describes, and the missing failure-mode specification means the carve-out cannot be implemented safely without Phase 3 inventing unreviewed, safety-critical behavior.
